From 48bd344e1040b9f2eb512be73c13f5db83efc191 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
Date: Thu, 9 Apr 2026 16:01:56 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] ALSA: usx2y: us144mkii: fix NULL deref on missing interface 0

A malicious USB device with the TASCAM US-144MKII device id can have a
configuration containing bInterfaceNumber=1 but no interface 0.  USB
configuration descriptors are not required to assign interface numbers
sequentially, so usb_ifnum_to_if(dev, 0) returns will NULL, which will
then be dereferenced directly.

Fix this up by checking the return value properly.

Cc: Jaroslav Kysela <perex@perex.cz>
Cc: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.com>
Fixes: dee1bcf28a3d ("ALSA: usb-audio: Add initial driver for TASCAM US-144MKII")
Cc: stable <stable@kernel.org>
Assisted-by: gregkh_clanker_t1000
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/2026040955-fall-gaining-e338@gregkh
Signed-off-by: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.de>

diff --git a/sound/usb/usx2y/us144mkii.c b/sound/usb/usx2y/us144mkii.c
index 0cf4fa74e210..94553b61013c 100644
--- a/sound/usb/usx2y/us144mkii.c
+++ b/sound/usb/usx2y/us144mkii.c
@@ -420,7 +420,11 @@ static int tascam_probe(struct usb_interface *intf,
 
 	/* The device has two interfaces; we drive both from this driver. */
 	if (intf->cur_altsetting->desc.bInterfaceNumber == 1) {
-		tascam = usb_get_intfdata(usb_ifnum_to_if(dev, 0));
+		struct usb_interface *intf_zero = usb_ifnum_to_if(dev, 0);
+
+		if (!intf_zero)
+			return -ENODEV;
+		tascam = usb_get_intfdata(intf_zero);
 		if (tascam) {
 			usb_set_intfdata(intf, tascam);
 			tascam->iface1 = intf;
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary

The patch fixes a null pointer dereference vulnerability in the TASCAM US-144MKII USB audio driver (`sound/usb/usx2y/us144mkii.c`). The bug occurred when a malicious USB device with the device ID of TASCAM US-144MKII had a configuration that included interface number 1 but lacked interface 0. In such a case, `usb_ifnum_to_if(dev, 0)` returns `NULL`, and the original code dereferenced this pointer directly without checking.

## Modifications

- **File: `sound/usb/usx2y/us144mkii.c`** (line 423, function `tascam_probe`):
  - Replaced the direct call `usb_get_intfdata(usb_ifnum_to_if(dev, 0))` with a two-step approach:
    1. Introduced a local variable `intf_zero` to hold the result of `usb_ifnum_to_if(dev, 0)`.
    2. Added a `NULL` check for `intf_zero`, returning `-ENODEV` if it is `NULL`.
    3. Only then does it proceed to call `usb_get_intfdata(intf_zero)`.

## Relationships

- The single change is confined to one file and one function.
- The fix directly addresses the root cause: missing validation of the return value before dereference.
- The change ensures robustness against malicious USB descriptors, preventing a kernel crash (NULL pointer dereference) and instead returning a proper error code (`-ENODEV`).
